lastCommit.message:
OTA-1855 — the emergency boot-gate cap loses the race it was never meant to win

MEASURED ON THE OWNER'S PIXEL 10 PRO XL / ANDROID 37, on OTA 2026-09-19-1850,
reported as "long lag on initial load":

    23:54:03.845  process starts
    23:54:04.001  OTA state = Checking
    23:54:12.354  character gate opens                 (+8.353s)
    23:54:14.008  OTA state = Error                    (+10.007s)

Two timers in the wrong order. App.tsx's emergency boot-gate cap was a bare
`8000` while the boot-front OTA check asked for `10_000`. 8 < 10, so on EVERY
launch the network could not answer, the emergency hatch fired FIRST and the
player paid a fixed eight-second stall at the splash before they could pick a
character — and the check then reported its own timeout two seconds later, into
a gate that had already opened without it.

The cap exists for a boot that is never coming back: hydrate() rejecting, or any
step throwing before the check resolves, would leave the gate locked forever and
brick the player out of their own saves. It is a stuck-boot escape hatch, NOT a
second OTA timeout, so it must lose every honest race.

THE 10s BUDGET IS PRESERVED, DELIBERATELY. It is OTA-1453's product decision for
cold radios, taken after two owner reports about missed updates; shortening it
back to 5s would "fix" the stall by reintroducing the fault that raised it.
Instead the cap is DERIVED:

    BOOT_OTA_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS  = 10_000
    OTA_GATE_SAFETY_MARGIN_MS  =  2_000
    OTA_GATE_SAFETY_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000   (the sum, by construction)

so the inversion is unrepresentable. That matters because of HOW it drifted:
OTA-405 wrote the 8s cap, OTA-1453 later raised the check 5s -> 10s, 120 lines
away in a different function, and nothing tied them together. Restored launch
ordering: check 10s < gate cap 12s < boot watchdog 25s.

The 2s margin only has to cover the JS between the check's timeout firing and
App.tsx setting otaBootResolved on the same tick. A larger margin would just be
a slower version of the same stall.

SCOPE: three constants and two call sites. No native change, no new binary, no
expo-updates or checkAndApplyOTA control-flow change, no hydration change, no
TitleScreen change. The 5s CLASSIFIER readiness cap (GATE B, a different timer
in a different file) is untouched and pinned as untouched.

STALE COMMENTS CORRECTED, both made stale by this defect and both of which made
8 > 5 look correct: App.tsx's cap note ("longer than the OTA check's own 5s
budget"), the BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS note ("past OTA-405's own 8s gate cap and the 5s
OTA budget"), and checkAndApplyOTA's option doc ("the boot-front gate uses a
shorter budget (~5s)").

TESTS: new suite ota1855TheCapLosesTheRace 10/10 — the 10s budget survives, the
cap is strictly greater, the derivation is a sum, the margin is small and real,
the cap cannot fire while the check is legitimately running, the escape hatch
still exists, the full ordering holds, a normal OTA failure still releases the
gate without the cap, the helper doc no longer claims ~5s, and the classifier
cap is untouched.

ota1174BugReportLoads' budget pin followed the value behind its new name. Its
claim is UNCHANGED — a budget exists and is bounded at both ends — only the
spelling moved, so it resolves one level of indirection instead of pinning a
literal that no longer sits at the call site.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: the derivation flipped to `-`, reproducing the shipped
8s-vs-10s inversion exactly. First run turned only ONE test red, and that was a
fault in the test: the helper recomputed `budget + margin` instead of reading
the shipped operator, so the invariant test stayed green through a real
inversion. Helper widened to read the operator; the control then turned FOUR
tests red including the invariant itself. Restored byte-identical (sha256
aede6e3ebf717afaf5dd2bb42d43caf04b21c14cb26191014aaac4bbcfeda5ce), green again.

VALIDATION: 22/22 local gates, typecheck source + test ratchet, full lint, and
the FULL FAST SURFACE 1350/1350 suites, 15,386 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.
Full-fast was run because this edits App.tsx, whose source an unknown number of
pins read — the same class that turned CI red on OTA-1854 an hour ago. No Heavy
CI.

NOT CLAIMED: no startup improvement is asserted until measured on the owner's
device. A slow or offline launch may still legitimately spend the full 10s
budget; what changed is that the emergency hatch can no longer fire before that
budget has had its chance.
